**What Happened**

At 2026-10-02T15:01:03Z, a high-severity KubePodCrashLooping alert fired for the `shop` service. Investigation of the live cluster found pod `frontend-d6db5d589-dn4kr` (part of the Deployment `frontend`) in CrashLoopBackOff status with 3 restarts, last terminated with Exit Code 1 [4, 7]. The Deployment showed READY 2/2, AVAILABLE 2, UP-TO-DATE 1/2, indicating only the newest pod was affected while the Deployment overall remained healthy [5, 8].

**Root Cause**

The root cause was a syntax error in the `frontend-nginx` ConfigMap: the directive `proxy_conect_timeout` (missing the "n" in "connect") is invalid, causing nginx to fail config validation at startup with `unknown directive "proxy_conect_timeout" in /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:9` [6, 9]. This typo is present in the ConfigMap's `last-applied-configuration` annotation, indicating it was introduced via a deliberate `kubectl apply` rather than a live edit [9]. A `kubectl rollout restart` was issued at 15:00:12 UTC, per the `kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt` annotation on the pod template, creating a new ReplicaSet (`frontend-d6db5d589`) whose pods read the already-broken ConfigMap on startup and failed immediately [7, 13]. The older ReplicaSet (`frontend-76d98597b9`) pods were already running prior to this and had the config loaded into their nginx master process in memory, so they never re-parsed the file and continued serving traffic normally, as shown by continuous 200 OK responses in their access logs [8, 12]. The timing of the restart annotation, pod creation, and first crash align closely, consistent with this causal chain [7, 13].

**Impact & Timeline**

This is a stuck rolling update rather than a full outage: the two old-revision pods remained healthy and serving all traffic (READY 2/2, AVAILABLE 2) while the single new-revision pod repeatedly crashed [5, 8, 12]. No correlated alerts or downstream service impact were identified [14, 15].

## shop/api KubePodCrashLooping - liveness probe port mismatch (2026-10-02 15:08 UTC)
Both `api` pods crash-looping (restart every ~60-70s, exit 137, "failed liveness probe, will be restarted"). Live Deployment spec has `livenessProbe.httpGet.port=8081` while `readinessProbe.port=8080` and the app (`api.py`, PORT env defaults to 8080, no override set) only listens on 8080 → liveness checks always get connection refused → kubelet kills+restarts container every cycle. The Deployment's `last-applied-configuration` annotation shows the originally-applied liveness port was 8080 (correct), but the live object was patched to 8081 — same untracked-imperative-edit anti-pattern as other shop-namespace incidents, this time via a probe-port change rather than env/image/configmap. NOT an OOM issue (Terminated Reason: Error, not OOMKilled) — distinct from the earlier shop/api log-shipper sidecar OOM incident (e68e36c8) which no longer applies (that sidecar container is gone from the current pod spec). Fix: patch/apply livenessProbe port back to 8080 to match readinessProbe, last-applied-config, and the app's actual port. Fifth distinct crash/rollout-stuck mechanism recorded in this namespace — reinforces the recurring anti-pattern of unreviewed imperative kubectl edits to live Deployment specs.

thoughts.content: Starting with history check per protocol — searching for prior shop/api crash loop incidents before fresh investigation.

Found 6 prior incidents in this namespace already — including one exact match: shop/api log-shipper sidecar OOM (e68e36c8, 14:44 UTC). That's my leading hypothesis, but per protocol I must disprove it with fresh evidence, not assume recurrence — this namespace has had 5+ distinct root causes already (image typo, missing secret, ConfigMap typo, BATCH_SIZE OOM, sidecar OOM). Let's check live cluster state now.

Hypothesis: shop/api pods are crash-looping now — need to check current pod status to confirm the symptom is actively occurring and identify the failing container/mechanism (don't assume it's the same log-shipper OOM as before).

All pods currently 1/1 Running, Ready 2/2 — not actively crash-looping right now. But both api pods show 1 restart within ~2min of age, worth checking why. Also notable: no log-shipper sidecar present this time (only single api container) — different from the prior incident's mechanism. Let's check events and pod history.

Critical finding: the kill reason is NOT OOM this time — it's Liveness probe failed: Get http://PodIP:8081/healthz: connection refused, causing kubelet to kill+restart the container repeatedly (Restart Count 2 in ~2.5min, matching "restarts every minute or so"). Readiness probe is on port 8080 (succeeds), but liveness probe targets port 8081. Let's check the Deployment spec and app code to see if the app actually listens on 8081.
Now checking: resource usage (rule out memory further), node health, and the previous ReplicaSet revision 1's probe config to determine exactly when the port 8081 misconfiguration was introduced.

Investigation Summary

Symptom confirmed CURRENTLY occurring: Both api pods (api-c7b987b4d-d8vj8, api-c7b987b4d-wtmf8) are actively restarting — Restart Count 2 and climbing within ~3.5 minutes, with "Killing" events logged 30-40s ago at time of investigation. This matches the alert's "restart every minute or so."

Root cause mechanism (CONFIRMED):
The live api Deployment spec has livenessProbe.httpGet.port: 8081, while readinessProbe correctly targets port 8080.
The app code (api-code ConfigMap, api.py) only binds ThreadingHTTPServer(("", PORT), H) where PORT defaults to 8080 — there is no PORT env var override in the Deployment (only REDIS_HOST=redis is set). The container never listens on 8081.
Every liveness check to :8081/healthz gets connection refused. After initialDelaySeconds: 15 + failureThreshold: 3 × periodSeconds: 10 ≈ 45–60s, kubelet kills the container ("Container api failed liveness probe, will be restarted", exit code 137) and restarts it — repeating indefinitely. This exactly matches the observed ~60-70s restart cadence on both pods.
Critically, the Deployment's kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration annotation — i.e., what was actually submitted via kubectl apply — specifies livenessProbe.port: 8080, matching the readiness probe and the app's real port. The live object has 8081, a value absent from the applied config. This is the same untracked-imperative-edit anti-pattern seen in prior shop-namespace incidents (missing Secret ref, image-tag typo) — someone patched/edited the live Deployment's liveness probe port directly, bypassing review.

Ruled out:
OOMKill: Last State: Terminated, Reason: Error (not OOMKilled); memory limit 128Mi un-exceeded; no OOM events in describe or namespace events. This differs from the earlier shop/api CrashLoopBackOff incident (e68e36c8) caused by a log-shipper sidecar OOM — that sidecar container doesn't even exist in the current pod spec (single api container only).
Node/cluster resource pressure: all 3 no

Conclusion: CONFIRMED

Root cause: The shop/api Deployment's live livenessProbe targets port 8081, but the api container only listens on port 8080 (per api.py source — PORT env defaults to 8080, no override set in the pod spec). Every liveness check gets connection refused, and kubelet kills+restarts the container on a ~45-60s cadence (initialDelaySeconds: 15 + failureThreshold: 3 × periodSeconds: 10), matching the reported "restarts every minute or so" exactly.

The Deployment's last-applied-configuration annotation (the tracked kubectl apply state) shows the liveness port was originally 8080 — correct and matching the readiness probe. The live object was changed to 8081 outside of that tracked apply, consistent with this namespace's recurring pattern of unreviewed imperative edits to live Deployment specs (5th distinct mechanism of this type found in shop).

Evidence:
describe pod on both api replicas: Liveness: http-get http://:8081/healthz vs Readiness: http-get http://:8080/healthz, repeated Unhealthy/Killing events firing within the last 30-40s, Restart Count actively incrementing.
api-code ConfigMap: app binds ThreadingHTTPServer(("", PORT), H), PORT defaults 8080, env only sets REDIS_HOST.
Deployment YAML: live spec port=8081 vs last-applied-configuration annotation port=8080 — proof of drift from the reviewed config.
Ruled out OOM: Last State: Terminated, Reason: Error (not OOMKilled), well under the 128Mi limit — differs from the earlier distinct log-shipper sidecar OOM incident on this same deployment (that sidecar no longer exists in the pod spec).
Ruled out node/cluster issues: all 3 nodes Ready; frontend, worker, redis, loadgen all healthy with 0 restarts — impact isolated to api.

Validated fix (not executed — blocked by read-only policy):
``
kubectl patch deployment api -n shop --type=json \
  -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/livenessProbe/httpGet/port","value":8080}]'
`
